text_blocks.snippet: Farxiga (dapagliflozin) is a medication that is approved for the treatment of type 2 diabetes. It is not currently approved for the treatment of prediabetes.
snippet_highlighted_words: It is not currently approved for the treatment of prediabetes

text_blocks.snippet: However, studies have shown that Farxiga may be beneficial for people with prediabetes. In one study, people with prediabetes who took Farxiga for 12 weeks had lower blood sugar levels and improved insulin sensitivity compared to those who took a placebo.

Farxiga works by increasing the amount of glucose (sugar) that is excreted in the urine. This can help to lower blood sugar levels. It may also help to improve insulin sensitivity and reduce the risk of developing type 2 diabetes.

If you are considering taking Farxiga for prediabetes, it is important to talk to your doctor. They can help you determine if this medication is right for you and discuss the potential risks and benefits.
Note: It is important to follow your doctor's instructions carefully when taking Farxiga. Do not take more or less than the prescribed dose.
